QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_14

question.text: 'Bharat Category II AIF' wishes to add a new external member to its Investment Committee AFTER investor on-boarding, whose name was NOT disclosed in the PPM. Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, what consent threshold is required from the investors?

answer.text: Simple majority — 51% by number of investors
Only SEBI approval is required, no investor consent
75% of investors by VALUE of investment in the AIF

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI Circular dated June 25, 2021 and SEBI (AIF) Regulations, an external IC member whose name was NOT in the PPM can be appointed only with consent of at least 75% of investors BY VALUE of investment. Ex-officio changes (e.g., Sponsor representative) don't need this consent. The Trap: Simple majority is too low. Unanimous is too high. SEBI-only consent ignores investor protection rationale. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C (All-Cat Manager) tests this 75%-by-value rule. This is distinctive of XIX-D (Cat I/II) and XIX-C — not relevant at Distributor level.
